## 4. Controlled Sub-Stage Decomposition of `CreatePipelineWithDriverCache` (Addressing D2 Point 1)

To separate raw driver compilation (`vkCreateGraphicsPipelines`) from `.vkpc` wrapper overhead (`CreateDriverCache`, `GetDriverCacheData`, `MakeEntry` FNV-1a checksum, and `Outcome::kStale` double-pass), we temporarily instrumented [`VulkanPipelineCache::CreatePipelineWithDriverCache`](../../tools/source/rexglue-sdk/src/graphics/vulkan/pipeline_cache.cpp#L569-L687) with `std::chrono::steady_clock` timers around every sub-step and ran four controlled scenarios on RTX 3060 Ti (`driver 621.14`) with `--fh1_frame_cost_csv` enabled (before reverting the temporary instrumentation):

### 4.1 Runtime PSO Creation: `--vulkan_store_pipeline_cache=true` (Default) vs. `false` (`VK_NULL_HANDLE`)

We deleted the title's `.xpso` / `.vkpc` files so that all **29 introductory/title-screen PSOs** (`6` on the CP thread + `23` on background lookahead threads across `14` active frames) were created during runtime while NVIDIA's internal `GLCache` already held the compiled shaders:

| Sub-Stage Inside `CreatePipelineWithDriverCache` ($N = 29$ identical runtime PSOs) | `--vulkan_store_pipeline_cache=true` (Default `.vkpc` Enabled) | `--vulkan_store_pipeline_cache=false` (`cache = VK_NULL_HANDLE`) | Delta / Overhead Caused by `.vkpc` Wrapper | Share of Default Runtime `CreatePipelineWithDriverCache` |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **1. `CreateDriverCache(nullptr, 0)`** (`vkCreatePipelineCache`) | `0.160 ms / PSO` | `0.000 ms / PSO` | `+0.160 ms / PSO` | `2.0%` |
| **2. `vkCreateGraphicsPipelines(device, cache, ...)`** | **`5.060 ms / PSO`** | **`0.199 ms / PSO`** (`0.191 ms` P50, `0.663 ms` max) | **`+4.861 ms / PSO`** *(NVIDIA driver populating `2.11 MB` into `cache`)* | `63.1%` (`2.5%` raw PSO + `60.6%` `cache` population) |
| **3. `GetDriverCacheData(cache)`** (`vkGetPipelineCacheData` x2 copying **`2,110,277 bytes`** + `vkDestroyPipelineCache`) | **`0.878 ms / PSO`** | `0.000 ms / PSO` | **`+0.878 ms / PSO`** | `10.9%` |
| **4. `driver_cache_file::MakeEntry` + `KeepDriverCacheEntry`** (single-byte FNV-1a checksum loop over `2.11 MB` at [`driver_cache_file.h:67`](../../tools/source/rexglue-sdk/src/graphics/vulkan/driver_cache_file.h#L67)) | **`1.920 ms / PSO`** | `0.000 ms / PSO` | **`+1.920 ms / PSO`** | `23.9%` |
| **Total `CreatePipelineWithDriverCache` per PSO (Mean / P50 / Max)** | **`8.021 ms`** (`7.530 ms` P50 / `16.382 ms` max) | **`0.200 ms`** (`0.191 ms` P50 / `0.663 ms` max) | **`+7.821 ms / PSO` (`40.1x` slower!)** | **`100.0%` (`97.5%` is `.vkpc` overhead!)** |
| **Sum of `bg_pipeline_ms` across all 14 active frames (`--fh1_frame_cost_csv`)** | **`226.80 ms`** | **`6.29 ms`** | **`+220.51 ms` (`36.1x` higher)** | — |

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Discovery Breakthrough (D2 Point 1)**: When NVIDIA's `GLCache` already has the shader compiled, raw `vkCreateGraphicsPipelines(device, VK_NULL_HANDLE, ...)` takes only **`0.199 ms / PSO`**. Passing an isolated temporary `VkPipelineCache` per pipeline in [`CreatePipelineWithDriverCache`](../../tools/source/rexglue-sdk/src/graphics/vulkan/pipeline_cache.cpp#L569-L687) forces the NVIDIA driver to merge/dump **`2.11 MB` (`2,110,277 bytes`)** of internal driver cache state into the temporary `VkPipelineCache` inside `vkCreateGraphicsPipelines` (`+4.861 ms`), copy `2.11 MB` out via `vkGetPipelineCacheData` (`+0.878 ms`), and hash `2.11 MB` byte-by-byte in `Checksum()` (`+1.920 ms`), turning a **`0.20 ms`** call into **`8.02 ms` (`40.1x` slower)**.

### 4.2 Startup Warm-Up Sub-Stage Breakdown (`Outcome::kReused` vs. `Outcome::kStale` vs. `512 MiB` Cap Overflow)

Running startup warm-up on the existing **342-pipeline** cache (`284` entries stored in the `535,813,834-byte` [511 MiB] `.vkpc` file, plus `58` unseeded overflow pipelines that exceeded `kMaxFileSize = 512 MiB`) across **6 worker threads** revealed the exact per-thread cost of all three code paths inside [`CreatePipelineWithDriverCache`](../../tools/source/rexglue-sdk/src/graphics/vulkan/pipeline_cache.cpp#L569-L687):

| Startup Warm-Up Path ($N = 342$ PSOs across 6 threads) | Count | Seed Blob Size | Pass 1: `CreateDriverCache` | Pass 1: `vkCreateGraphicsPipelines` | Pass 1: `GetDriverCacheData` | Pass 2 (`kStale`): `CreateDriverCache(nullptr)` | Pass 2 (`kStale`): 2nd `vkCreateGraphicsPipelines` | Pass 2 (`kStale`): 2nd `GetDriverCacheData` | `MakeEntry` (FNV-1a Checksum on `2.15 MB`) | Total per PSO on Worker Thread (Mean / P50) | Wall-Clock Share Across 6 Threads |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **1. Seeded Hit (`Outcome::kReused`)** | `33` | `23.1 KB` (`15–90 KB`) | `0.233 ms` | **`0.228 ms`** | `0.062 ms` *(skipped on hit)* | `0.000 ms` | `0.000 ms` | `0.000 ms` | `0.000 ms` | **`0.523 ms`** (`0.262 ms` P50) | `~0.09 ms / PSO` |
| **2. Seeded Miss (`Outcome::kStale` Double-Pass)** | **`251`** | **`2.15 MB`** | `0.913 ms` | **`5.329 ms`** | **`1.601 ms`** (`2.15 MB` copy) | `0.246 ms` | **`10.258 ms`** | **`1.507 ms`** (`2.14 MB` copy) | **`2.387 ms`** | **`22.241 ms`** (`21.856 ms` P50; **`64.7%` in Pass 2!**) | `~3.71 ms / PSO` |
| **3. Unseeded 512 MiB Overflow (`Outcome::kStored`, then Discarded)** | **`58`** | `0 B` *(omitted by 512 MiB cap)* | `0.340 ms` | **`11.010 ms`** | **`1.491 ms`** (`2.15 MB` copy) | `0.000 ms` | `0.000 ms` | `0.000 ms` | **`2.498 ms`** | **`15.339 ms`** (`15.174 ms` P50; **`2.15 MB` blob then discarded!**) | `~2.56 ms / PSO` |

**Why did `251` seeded entries hit `Outcome::kStale` and why did `58` entries have `0 B` seed?**
- Inspection of `.vkpc` entries on disk shows that entries #0–#32 (`33` entries) are small (`15–90 KB`) and hit `Outcome::kReused` in **`0.26 ms` P50**. Entries #33–#283 (`251` entries) are **`2.15 MB` each** (`251 * 2.15 MB = 535.0 MB`), exhausting the `512 MiB` budget at entry #283 (`284` total).
- Furthermore, when `--resolution_scale` is toggled between `1` and `2` across developer sessions, `SpirvShaderTranslator` emits different SPIR-V instructions for scaled render targets, while `PipelineDescription::GetHash()` (`key`) does **not** include `draw_resolution_scale_x/y`. Thus the `.vkpc` key matches, `VkPipelineCreationFeedback` reports `0` (`kStale`), and [`CreatePipelineWithDriverCache`](../../tools/source/rexglue-sdk/src/graphics/vulkan/pipeline_cache.cpp#L655-L677) executes the **`22.24 ms/PSO` double-compilation and double-extraction pass**!
- Even worse, for the remaining **`58` pipelines** (`#284–#341`), `CreatePipelineWithDriverCache` still creates a temporary `VkPipelineCache`, pays `11.01 ms` in `vkCreateGraphicsPipelines` + `1.49 ms` in `GetDriverCacheData` + `2.50 ms` in `MakeEntry` checksum (`15.34 ms/PSO`) to produce a `2.15 MB` entry, and then [`KeepDriverCacheEntry`](../../tools/source/rexglue-sdk/src/graphics/vulkan/pipeline_cache.cpp#L714-L723) **throws that `2.15 MB` entry away** because `driver_cache_bytes_ + entry.data.size() > kMaxFileSize`!

---

## 5. Resolving the Startup vs. Runtime Scale Discrepancy & Per-Frame vs. Per-PSO Conflation (D2 Points 2 & 3)

### 5.1 Why Startup Warm-Up (`0.55–8.4 ms/PSO` wall-clock) Differs by 3x–10x from Runtime Slow Frames (`191.88 ms/slow frame`)

The apparent discrepancy between startup PSO warm-up numbers and runtime `pipeline_ms` is completely explained by three factors:

1. **Startup warm-up logs in the dataset (`SHADER_WARMUP: Vulkan complete in 1,359–3,133 ms`) were running with a WARM NVIDIA `GLCache`, dominated by `.vkpc` disk I/O and `.vkpc` `2.15 MB` blob overhead**:
   - In warm `.vkpc` startup runs ([`runtime-20261109-183049.log:214-230`](../../game-data/runtime/logs/runtime-20261109-183049.log#L214-L230), [`183708.log:214-229`](../../game-data/runtime/logs/runtime-20261109-183708.log#L214-L229), total `1,416–1,419 ms` for `339` PSOs):
     - **`951–954 ms` (`67.3%`)** happens **before** shader translation or PSO creation even starts — inside `driver_cache_file::Load` reading and FNV-1a checksum-verifying the **`535.8 MB` `.vkpc` file** from disk!
     - **`275–279 ms` (`19.5%`)** is single-threaded startup guest shader translation ([`vulkan/pipeline_cache.cpp:1021-1039`](../../tools/source/rexglue-sdk/src/graphics/vulkan/pipeline_cache.cpp#L1021-L1039)).
     - Only **`186–190 ms` (`13.2%`, `0.55 ms/PSO` wall-clock across 6 threads)** is spent in the PSO creation loop (`284` reused at `~0.5 ms/thread` + `55` overflow at `~15 ms/thread` across 6 threads).
   - In stale/rebuilt `.vkpc` startup runs ([`runtime-20261108-165454.log:214-228`](../../game-data/runtime/logs/runtime-20261108-165454.log#L214-L228), `3,133 ms` total, `2,819 ms` PSO phase for `334` PSOs = `8.44 ms/PSO` wall-clock across 6 threads), the worker threads were spending **`15–23 ms/PSO` per thread** doing `Outcome::kStale` double-pass `2.15 MB` `.vkpc` serialization (Section 4.2) while NVIDIA's `GLCache` already held the SASS machine code.
2. **True cold runtime PSO misses (`GLCache` cold) must compile SPIR-V to SASS machine code for the first time (`46.8–205.3 ms / PSO`)**:
   - When a brand-new shader/PSO combination is encountered during gameplay for the very first time, NVIDIA's `GLCache` does not have it.
   - Isolating slow-frame windows where **exactly 1 PSO was built on the CP thread with 0 lookahead waits (`slowCount == 1`, `pipelines == 1.0`, `waits delta == 0`)** gives the true single-PSO cold runtime cost (`vkCreateGraphicsPipelines` + `~8 ms` `.vkpc` overhead):
     - [`runtime-20261108-161438.log:377`](../../game-data/runtime/logs/runtime-20261108-161438.log#L377): `1` PSO, `0` waits $\rightarrow$ **`46.8 ms`**
     - [`runtime-20261108-161438.log:468`](../../game-data/runtime/logs/runtime-20261108-161438.log#L468): `1` PSO, `0` waits $\rightarrow$ **`101.5 ms`**
     - [`runtime-20261108-161438.log:459`](../../game-data/runtime/logs/runtime-20261108-161438.log#L459): `1` PSO, `0` waits $\rightarrow$ **`112.2 ms`**
     - [`runtime-20261109-152130.log:1367`](../../game-data/runtime/logs/runtime-20261109-152130.log#L1367): `1` PSO, `0` waits $\rightarrow$ **`195.6 ms`**
     - [`runtime-20261108-161438.log:413`](../../game-data/runtime/logs/runtime-20261108-161438.log#L413): `1` PSO, `0` waits $\rightarrow$ **`205.3 ms`**
   - This **`46.8–205.3 ms / PSO`** single-PSO cold compilation range on Vulkan matches single-threaded cold D3D12 `CreateGraphicsPipelineState` (**`75.02–81.04 ms / PSO` mean** across 112 PSOs in [`runtime-20261108-160653.log:27`](../../game-data/runtime/logs/runtime-20261108-160653.log#L27) and [`163340.log:27`](../../game-data/runtime/logs/runtime-20261108-163340.log#L27)) plus `~8 ms` of `.vkpc` serialization and runtime driver lock contention with active command-buffer submission.
3. **Why "per slow frame" (`191.88 ms`) is higher than average "per PSO" (`43.91 ms`)**:
   - **Multi-PSO lookahead batching in a single frame**: As shown in Section 3.1, [`ConfigurePipeline`](../../tools/source/rexglue-sdk/src/graphics/vulkan/pipeline_cache.cpp#L1845-L1927) includes `finish_ahead` (`Fh1WaitForAhead`) inside `pipeline_ms`, which waits for **all $K$ background lookahead PSOs** queued during that command buffer walk while counting only `0` or `1` in `fh1_frame_cost::Current().pipelines`.
   - **Selection bias (`kSlowMs = 50.0 ms`)**: `fh1_frame_cost::Report` only includes frames whose total frame time reached `>= 50 ms`. Fast runtime PSO misses (`< 17 ms`, such as warm-`GLCache` misses at `8.02 ms`) do not trigger a `>= 50 ms` frame and are excluded from `GPU slow frames`.

### 5.2 Complete Session-Level Decomposition: Per-Slow-Frame vs. Per-PSO in `runtime-20261108-161438.log`

In the primary 15-minute cold Vulkan gameplay session ([`game-data/runtime/logs/runtime-20261108-161438.log:315-487`](../../game-data/runtime/logs/runtime-20261108-161438.log#L315-L487)), the engine started with `165` preloaded PSOs and finished with `332` PSOs — building **`167` new runtime PSOs** in total (`59` inline on the CP thread + `108` on background lookahead threads):

| Metric (`runtime-20261108-161438.log`, 15-minute Cold Vulkan Session) | Value | Notes / Code Citation |
| :--- | ---: | :--- |
| **Total new runtime PSOs created** | **`167` PSOs** | `332 total - 165 preload` ([`line 487`](../../game-data/runtime/logs/runtime-20261108-161438.log#L487)) |
| — Created on background lookahead threads (`ahead`) | **`108` PSOs (`64.7%`)** | Queued by `Fh1PipelineLookahead` (`109 queued`) |
| — Created inline on CP thread (`inline`) | **`59` PSOs (`35.3%`)** | Only `23` of these occurred inside `>= 50 ms` slow-frame windows (`pipelines` counter) |
| **Total slow-frame `pipeline_ms` across all 37 slow frames in session** | **`7,333.4 ms`** | Mean **`198.20 ms / slow frame`** (`37` slow frames across `15` windows) |
| — Portion spent in `Fh1WaitForAhead` (`finish_ahead` waiting on `108` ahead PSOs) | **`4,348.7 ms` (`59.3%`)** | `60` waits (`72.48 ms / wait`, or **`40.27 ms / ahead PSO`**) |
| — Portion spent in direct CP-thread `EnsurePipelineCreated` (`59` inline PSOs) | **`2,984.7 ms` (`40.7%`)** | **`50.59 ms / inline CP PSO`** averaged across all 59 inline PSOs |
| **True Session Mean Slow-Frame Stall per Runtime PSO (`7,333.4 ms / 167 PSOs`)** | **`43.91 ms / PSO`** | Compare with **`198.20 ms / slow frame`** (`~4.51 PSOs` amortized per slow frame) |

Even within a single 10-second burst (e.g., [`line 343`](../../game-data/runtime/logs/runtime-20261108-161438.log#L343)–[`345`](../../game-data/runtime/logs/runtime-20261108-161438.log#L345) at `16:15:58`, entering a new zone), the log records **`9` slow frames** averaging **`195.9 ms / slow frame`** (`1,763.1 ms` total `pipeline_ms`), while [`line 345`](../../game-data/runtime/logs/runtime-20261108-161438.log#L345) shows that **`32` new PSOs** (`23` ahead + `9` inline) were created during that window — meaning each slow frame bundled **`3.56 PSOs`**, and the true cost per PSO in that burst was **`55.10 ms / PSO`** (`1,763.1 ms / 32 PSOs`), not `195.9 ms / PSO`!

## 7. D3D12 Distributions, Patch Verification (`d3d12-blocking-pso-precompile.patch`), and Thread-Normalized Ratios (D2 Points 4 & 5)

### 7.1 Verification of `patches/rexglue-0.10.0/d3d12-blocking-pso-precompile.patch` vs. `tools/source/rexglue-sdk`

1. **What the patch fixes**: [`patches/rexglue-0.10.0/d3d12-blocking-pso-precompile.patch:12-22`](../../patches/rexglue-0.10.0/d3d12-blocking-pso-precompile.patch#L12-L22) fixes [`d3d12::PipelineCache::InitializeShaderStorage`](../../tools/source/rexglue-sdk/src/graphics/d3d12/pipeline_cache.cpp#L537) by changing:
   ```cpp
   while (creation_threads_.size() < creation_thread_original_count) {
   ```
   to:
   ```cpp
   while (creation_threads_.size() < creation_thread_needed_count) {
   ```
   and moving `if (await_creation_completion_event)` outside `if (!creation_threads_.empty())` so startup PSO creation runs in parallel across `logical_processor_count - 1` worker threads even when `async_shader_compilation=false`.
2. **Why `tools/source/rexglue-sdk/src/graphics/d3d12/pipeline_cache.cpp:537` currently does NOT have the patch**:
   - Prior to **`2026-11-08 15:58:13`** (commit `3954dec`, *"feat(vulkan): integrate ReIGlue SDK and frame capture validation"*), the repository built upstream `rexglue-sdk v0.10.0` via [`scripts/prepare-sdk-source.ps1`](../../scripts/prepare-sdk-source.ps1#L45-L62), which **applied [`patches/rexglue-0.10.0/d3d12-blocking-pso-precompile.patch`](../../patches/rexglue-0.10.0/d3d12-blocking-pso-precompile.patch)**.
   - In commit `3954dec` (`2026-11-08 15:58:13`), `tools/source/rexglue-sdk` was switched to the `ReIGlue` repository (`a5fd408` + local commits `875ce25`, `4c4f222`, `e38fb9a` adding `SHADER_WARMUP:` logs), and **`d3d12-blocking-pso-precompile.patch` was not ported to the `ReIGlue` checkout**.
3. **Exact identification of which D3D12 logs ran WITH vs. WITHOUT the patch**:
   - **Pre-`2026-11-08 15:58` logs (WITH patch — multi-threaded Stage b across $N$ threads, no `SHADER_WARMUP:` log line)**: `11` of the `13` cold/rebuilt D3D12 startup runs (plus `runtime-20261108-175858.log`, which launched an earlier `majin_recomp_usa.exe` binary without `SHADER_WARMUP:`).
   - **Post-`2026-11-08 15:58` logs (WITHOUT patch — single-threaded Stage b on `1` thread, contains `SHADER_WARMUP: D3D12` log line)**: [`runtime-20261108-160653.log:24-28`](../../game-data/runtime/logs/runtime-20261108-160653.log#L24-L28) (`9,076 ms` for `112` PSOs = **`81.036 ms / PSO`**) and [`runtime-20261108-163340.log:24-28`](../../game-data/runtime/logs/runtime-20261108-163340.log#L24-L28) (`8,402 ms` for `112` PSOs = **`75.018 ms / PSO`**).

### 7.2 Thread-Normalized D3D12 Stage (b) vs. Stage (a) Comparison (Addressing D2 Point 4)

Because Stage (a) (`Translated X shaders`) always runs across $N = \text{logical\_processor\_count} - 1$ threads ([`d3d12/pipeline_cache.cpp:478-486`](../../tools/source/rexglue-sdk/src/graphics/d3d12/pipeline_cache.cpp#L478-L486)), comparing Stage (a) against unpatched single-threaded Stage (b) (`9,076 ms / 12 ms = 756:1`) inflates the wall-clock ratio by the thread count ($N$). Separating **Patched (N threads vs. N threads)** from **Unpatched (1 thread vs. N threads)** gives the true apples-to-apples ratio:

| D3D12 Cold / Rebuilt Startup Group | Runs ($N$) | Stage (a) Threads | Stage (b) Threads | Stage (a) `ms / shader` Wall-Clock | Stage (b) `ms / PSO` Wall-Clock | **Apples-to-Apples Per-Item Ratio (`ms/PSO : ms/shader`)** | Total Startup Stage (b)Share |
| :--- | ---: | :--- | :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **Patched (`d3d12-blocking-pso-precompile.patch` APPLIED)** | `11` | $N$ threads | **$N$ threads** | `0.027–0.072 ms` (`0.033 ms` P50) | **`6.49–11.99 ms / PSO`** (`7.67 ms` P50; `1,506–3,308 ms` for `180–295` PSOs) | **`166:1 – 240:1`** (`214:1` P50; `9.9:1` in 1 partial-warm run) | **`97.8% – 99.7%`** |
| **Unpatched (Post-`3954dec` `ReIGlue` WITHOUT patch)** | `2` | $N$ threads | **`1` thread** *(line 537 bug)* | `0.070–0.094 ms` | **`75.02–81.04 ms / PSO`** (`8,402–9,076 ms` for `112` PSOs) | *`862:1 – 1,072:1` (unnormalized wall-clock; **`~80:1 – 150:1` per-thread**)* | **`99.9%`** |
| **Warm `DXCache` Startup Runs** | `92` | $N$ threads | $N$ or `1` thread | `0.032 ms` P50 (`6.0 ms` total) | **`0.149 ms / PSO`** P50 (`39.0 ms` P50 total for `215–276` PSOs) | **`4.7 : 1`** P50 | **`86.4%`** P50 (`86.5%` mean) |

## 8. Summary of Architectural & Implementation Fixes Unlocked by D2

1. **Fix or Disable Per-Pipeline `.vkpc` Mega-Blobs in `VulkanPipelineCache` ([`vulkan/pipeline_cache.cpp:569-725`](../../tools/source/rexglue-sdk/src/graphics/vulkan/pipeline_cache.cpp#L569-L725))**:
   - The current per-pipeline `VkPipelineCache` design in `CreatePipelineWithDriverCache` has an explicit SDK comment noting `~2 MB` per entry on NVIDIA ([`line 695`](../../tools/source/rexglue-sdk/src/graphics/vulkan/pipeline_cache.cpp#L695)). Our controlled probe proves this design:
     - Adds **`+7.82 ms / PSO` (`40.1x` slowdown)** to every runtime PSO creation when `GLCache` is warm (`8.02 ms` vs. `0.20 ms` with `VK_NULL_HANDLE`).
     - Adds **`851–954 ms`** of blocking disk read + FNV-1a checksum time on every startup (`535.8 MB` `.vkpc` file).
     - Caps out at **283–284 pipelines (`512 MiB`)**, forcing all subsequent pipelines (`55–58` PSOs in current logs) to pay `15.34 ms/PSO` per thread on every boot only to have their `2.15 MB` blobs discarded!
     - Wastes **`22.24 ms/PSO` per thread** (`64.7%` in the 2nd pass) whenever `Outcome::kStale` triggers (e.g., resolution scale changes, because `draw_resolution_scale` is omitted from the `.vkpc` entry key).
   - Replacing per-PSO `.vkpc` blobs with a **single shared device-wide `VkPipelineCache`** (merged/saved once at shutdown) or relying on NVIDIA's native `GLCache` (`--vulkan_store_pipeline_cache=false`) eliminates all four overheads immediately without pre-compiling anything.
2. **Re-apply [`patches/rexglue-0.10.0/d3d12-blocking-pso-precompile.patch`](../../patches/rexglue-0.10.0/d3d12-blocking-pso-precompile.patch) to the `ReIGlue` SDK checkout ([`d3d12/pipeline_cache.cpp:537`](../../tools/source/rexglue-sdk/src/graphics/d3d12/pipeline_cache.cpp#L537))**:
   - Restores multi-threaded D3D12 startup PSO creation, cutting cold startup PSO compile time from `75–81 ms / PSO` (`9.1 s` for `112` PSOs) back down to `6.5–12.0 ms / PSO` (`1.5–3.3 s` for `180–295` PSOs).
3. **True First-Run Cold PSO Compilation (`46.8–205.3 ms / PSO` on Vulkan, `75–81 ms / PSO` single-threaded on D3D12) Still Requires Pre-Compilation / Warm-Up or Async Mitigation**:
   - Even with `.vkpc` fixed (`0.20 ms / PSO` when `GLCache` is warm), a player's **first and only playthrough** starts with a **cold driver `GLCache`/`DXCache`**, where each unseen PSO costs **`~45–205 ms`** to compile into GPU machine code (`SASS`). Therefore, D3–D7 remain essential to eliminate first-run in-game compilation stalls.

# D3 — Pipeline Population & Growth Curve (`pipeline-population`)

- **Date:** 2026-11-10
- **Status:** Complete (with partial game coverage caveat)
- **Reproducible script:** [`scripts/discovery/d3-pipeline-population.mjs`](../../scripts/discovery/d3-pipeline-population.mjs)
- **Plan question ([`docs/SHADER_PRECOMPILATION_PLAN.md`](../SHADER_PRECOMPILATION_PLAN.md#L106)):**
  > *"How many distinct pipelines/shaders does the game use, and does that count plateau?"*

---

## 1. Executive Summary

1. **Total population observed in on-disk binary caches (`7` `.xsh` files and `8` `.xpso` files):**
   - **Unique guest shaders (global `union` of all `.xsh` files and all `203` logs):** **`242` unique Xenos shaders** (**`100` vertex shaders** + **`142` pixel shaders**), totaling only **`~266 KB`** of raw Xenos microcode (mean of **`1,102.2 bytes` / `275.6 dwords`** per shader; minimum `36 bytes`, maximum `7,008 bytes`).
   - **Zero duplicate records in `.xsh`:** all `7` `.xsh` files contain `0` duplicate records. All `80` VS hashes and `105` PS hashes emitted in historical log lines (`Creating graphics pipeline state`) are present in on-disk `.xsh` files (`100%` shader retention).
   - **Unique PSO descriptions (`.xpso`) in cumulative primary caches:**
     - **Vulkan FBO ([`4E4D0816.fbo.vk.xpso`](../../game-data/runtime/cache/vulkan-vulkan/release/shaders/shareable/4E4D0816.fbo.vk.xpso)):** **`342` unique PSOs** (`23,276 bytes`), referencing **`230` unique shaders** (`97` VS + `133` PS), **`14` depth-only pipelines (`PS = 0`)**, **`183` unique `(VS, PS)` pairs**, **`195` unique `(VS_mod, PS_mod)` tuples**, and **`94` unique fixed-state/render-pass blocks** (**mean of `1.87 PSOs` per `(VS, PS)` pair**, maximum `20`).
     - **D3D12 RTV ([`4E4D0816.rtv.d3d12.xpso`](../../game-data/runtime/cache/d3d12-default/release/shaders/shareable/4E4D0816.rtv.d3d12.xpso)):** **`295` unique PSOs** (`21,252 bytes`), referencing **`220` unique shaders** (`94` VS + `126` PS), **`12` depth-only pipelines (`PS = 0`)**, **`177` unique `(VS, PS)` pairs**, **`190` unique `(VS_mod, PS_mod)` tuples**, and **`68` unique fixed-state blocks** (**mean of `1.67 PSOs` per `(VS, PS)` pair**, maximum `12`).
     - **Vulkan FSI ([`4E4D0816.fsi.vk.xpso`](../../game-data/runtime/cache/vulkan-vulkan/release/shaders/shareable/4E4D0816.fsi.vk.xpso)) and D3D12 ROV ([`4E4D0816.rov.d3d12.xpso`](../../game-data/runtime/cache/d3d12-rov/release/shaders/shareable/4E4D0816.rov.d3d12.xpso)):** **`168` PSOs** (`136` `(VS, PS)` pairs, only `15` fixed-state blocks, **`1.24 PSOs/pair`**) and **`143` PSOs** (`121` `(VS, PS)` pairs, only `13` fixed-state blocks, **`1.18 PSOs/pair`**). In FSI/ROV paths (where blending and EDRAM depth/stencil are resolved in the pixel shader via interlock/ROV rather than pipeline fixed-function state), the combinatorial state multiplier per `(VS, PS)` pair drops from `1.67–1.87x` to **`1.18–1.24x`**.
2. **High overlap across backends (`Vulkan FBO` vs `D3D12 RTV`):**
   - Of the `230` shaders used in Vulkan FBO and `220` in D3D12 RTV, **`208` shaders (`86.0%` of the union of `242` shaders) are identical** across both backends.
   - Of the `183` `(VS, PS)` pairs in Vulkan FBO and `177` in D3D12 RTV, **`163` pairs (`82.7%` of the union of `197` on-disk pairs) are identical**.
   - Additionally, the `d3d12-rtv` cache (`157` PSOs) is an **exact `100%` subset (`157/157`)** of the `XXH3_64bits` hashes of `PipelineDescription` present in `d3d12-default` (`295` PSOs), confirming that `PipelineDescription` is deterministic across runs along the same route.
3. **Growth dynamics and plateaus (within zones vs between zones):**
   - **Sharp local plateaus within each explored zone:** In the longest continuous session ([`runtime-20261108-161438.log`](../../game-data/runtime/logs/runtime-20261108-161438.log), `15.9 min`), growth occurs in **concentrated steps during zone/cutscene transitions**, interspersed by **multi-minute plateaus**:
     - Minutes 1–2 (opening cutscene + entry into Zone 1): `165 → 229` PSOs (`+64` PSOs, `+19` shaders).
     - **Plateau 1 (Minutes 3–4, exploring Zone 1):** `229 → 236` PSOs (**`+7` PSOs in 2 minutes and `+0` new shaders** — fixed at `202` shaders).
     - Minute 5 (sub-area transition / combat): `236 → 267` PSOs (`+31` PSOs, `+2` shaders).
     - **Plateau 2 (Minutes 6–9, 4 minutes of continuous gameplay):** `267 → 275` PSOs (**only `+8` PSOs and `+5` shaders in 4 minutes = `2.0 PSOs/min`**).
     - Minutes 10–12 (new main area + meeting the Majin / Achievement `#2`): `275 → 327` PSOs (`+52` PSOs, `+22` shaders).
     - **Plateau 3 (Minutes 13–15, 3 minutes continuous + 2nd cutscene):** `327 → 332` PSOs (**only `+5` PSOs and `+4` shaders in 3 minutes = `1.7 PSOs/min`**).
   - **Stabilization across previously visited routes in subsequent sessions:** Across the next 6 Vulkan sessions spanning 2 days (`2026-11-08 16:31` to `2026-11-09 18:37`), the cache grew only from `332 → 334 → 335 → 339 → 342` PSOs (**`+10` total PSOs**), with entire sessions of `63–89 s` logging **`0` new PSOs and `0.0 ms` wait time**. On D3D12, the final sessions on `2026-11-08` grew from `291 → 293 → 295` PSOs with **`+0` new shaders** (stationary at `220` shaders).
   - **Sublinearity of shaders relative to PSOs:** As the cache expands from `100` to `342` PSOs in Vulkan FBO, the `PSOs / Shader` ratio increases from **`0.97`** (`100` PSOs for `103` shaders) to **`1.49`** (`342` PSOs for `230` shaders), and the `PSOs / (VS, PS) Pair` ratio rises from **`1.32`** to **`1.87`**. This demonstrates that new PSOs in later areas increasingly reuse previously known shaders under new combinations of fixed-state/render passes.
4. **Critical caveat — Local plateau vs whole game coverage:**
   - Existing caches cover the early game (menu, opening cutscenes, and the first `~3–4` playable areas up to meeting the Majin / Achievement `#2`). Therefore, the figures of **`242` shaders** and **`342` PSOs (Vulkan FBO) / `295` PSOs (D3D12 RTV)** represent a **local plateau along the tested routes**, **not** a `100%` ceiling of the full campaign.
   - Nevertheless, the scale of *Majin and the Forsaken Kingdom*'s engine remains modest (hundreds of shaders and a few hundred to ~1,000 PSOs estimated across the entire campaign, rather than tens of thousands), making local on-disk precompilation viable if the pipeline list is available. On D3D12 with multi-threaded precompilation active, warm pre-pass takes `~2–3 s` for `300` PSOs; on Vulkan without `.vkpc` wrapper overhead, it takes `< 100 ms` with warm driver cache, or `~6 s` in parallel with completely cold driver cache (empirically measured).

## 2. Binary Format of Analyzed Caches (SDK Source Code)

Direct parsing in [`scripts/discovery/d3-pipeline-population.mjs`](../../scripts/discovery/d3-pipeline-population.mjs) follows the exact SDK C++ structures:

1. **Guest Shader Storage File (`4E4D0816.xsh`)** — defined in [`pipeline_store_file.h:35-69`](../../tools/source/rexglue-sdk/include/rex/graphics/pipeline_store_file.h#L35-L69):
   - `8-byte` header (`ShaderStorageFileHeader`): `magic = 0x48534558` (`'XESH'`), `version_swapped = 0x19122020` (`SwapBytes(0x20201219)`).
   - Variable-length record sequence: `12-byte` `ShaderStoredHeader` (`uint64_t ucode_data_hash`, `uint32_t ucode_dword_count : 31`, `xenos::ShaderType type : 1`, where `0 = kVertex` and `1 = kPixel` per [`xenos.h:33-36`](../../tools/source/rexglue-sdk/include/rex/graphics/xenos.h#L33-L36)) followed by `ucode_dword_count * 4` bytes of Xenos microcode.
2. **Vulkan Pipeline Description File (`4E4D0816.<fbo|fsi>.vk.xpso`)** — defined in [`vulkan/pipeline_cache.h:141-272`](../../tools/source/rexglue-sdk/include/rex/graphics/vulkan/pipeline_cache.h#L141-L272):
   - `20-byte` header (`Format 2`, with `version_2_marker = 0xFFFFFFFF`, `description_version_swapped = SwapBytes(0x20260228)`, `modification_version_swapped = SwapBytes(0x20261018)`) in `.fbo.vk.xpso` files, or legacy `12-byte` header in `.fsi.vk.xpso` files.
   - Fixed **`68-byte`** records (`PipelineStoredDescription`): `8 bytes` of `description_hash` (`XXH3_64bits`) + `60 bytes` of `PipelineDescription`:
     - `vertex_shader_hash` (`8B`), `vertex_shader_modification` (`8B`), `pixel_shader_hash` (`8B`), `pixel_shader_modification` (`8B`);
     - `render_pass_key` (`4B`, [`vulkan/render_target_cache.h:36-78`](../../tools/source/rexglue-sdk/include/rex/graphics/vulkan/render_target_cache.h#L36-L78));
     - `8B` of rasterization/depth/stencil registers (`depth_bias`, `depth_bias_slope_scaled`, bitfields for topology, cull mode, depth/stencil, etc.) + `16B` of `PipelineRenderTarget[4]` (blend/color write mask).
3. **D3D12 Pipeline Description File (`4E4D0816.<rtv|rov>.d3d12.xpso`)** — defined in [`d3d12/pipeline_cache.h:101-228`](../../tools/source/rexglue-sdk/include/rex/graphics/d3d12/pipeline_cache.h#L101-L228):
   - `12-byte` header (`magic = 'XEPS'`, `magic_api = 'DXRT'` or `'DXRO'`, `version_swapped = SwapBytes(0x20260226)`).
   - Fixed **`72-byte`** records (`PipelineStoredDescription`): `8 bytes` of `description_hash` (`XXH3_64bits`) + `64 bytes` of `PipelineDescription` (`vertex_shader_hash`, `vertex_shader_modification`, `pixel_shader_hash`, `pixel_shader_modification`, `depth_bias`, `depth_bias_slope_scaled`, `8B` fixed-state bitfields, and `16B` `PipelineRenderTarget[4]`).

**Technical reading of curves:**
- During the first `100` PSOs (boot, menus, opening cutscene), almost every PSO introduces a new shader (`100` PSOs for `103` shaders; `0.97 PSO/shader`).

The remaining `70` PSOs are **recombinations of already loaded shaders** with different blend, depth/stencil, or `RenderPassKey` masks.

#### D3D12 Main Path (`4E4D0816.rtv.d3d12.xpso`)
1. `2026-11-06`: grows progressively from `0 → 151` (`131` shaders) → `177` (`152` shaders) → `180` (`154` shaders) → `215` (`182` shaders) → `223` (`185` shaders).
2. `2026-11-07`: grows from `227` (`188` shaders) → `237` (`192` shaders) → `268` (`203` shaders, in a session of `256.1 s` / `4.3 min`) → `276` (`209` shaders).
3. `2026-11-08`: reaches `291` PSOs (`220` shaders) → `293` PSOs (`220` shaders, session of `99.7 s`) → **`295` PSOs (`220` shaders)**, stabilizing with **`+0` new shaders** across the final three sessions.

---

## 6. Methodological Caveats and Implications for the Plan (D4–D7)

1. **Proven local plateau vs partial campaign coverage:**
   - Data confirms that the pipeline population **reaches rapid plateaus within each zone** (rates of `0` to `2 PSOs/min` after the first `30–60 s` entering an area) and **heavily reuses the same shader set** (`242` unique shaders across testing history).
   - However, all recorded sessions traverse the early game (up to meeting the Majin / Achievement `#2`). Intermediate and late areas, new elemental Majin powers (wind, lightning, fire, purification), and later bosses will add new shaders and PSOs.
   - **Full game projection:** For a mid-scope Xbox 360 title like *Majin and the Forsaken Kingdom*, with `~242` shaders and `~342` PSOs covering menus + cutscenes + first areas + core mechanics, the full campaign is projected in the range of **`~350–600` unique shaders** and **`~600–1,200` PSOs** (extrapolation based on initial discovery rate, not a final 100% campaign measurement).
2. **Direct impact on local precompilation feasibility (warm-up):**
   - At the scale of the current `342` PSOs (or even `~1,000` PSOs in the full game):
     - The `.xsh` (`~266 KB`) and `.xpso` (`~23 KB`) files are tiny and load instantaneously.
     - On **Vulkan**, with warm NVIDIA driver cache (`GLCache`) and without `.vkpc` CPU wrapper overhead, creating `342` PSOs costs only **`0.05–0.20 ms/PSO` wall-clock** (`17–68 ms` for `342` PSOs; verified at `274 ms` total startup in [`game-data/runtime/logs/d4-warm-warmup-pass2.log`](../../game-data/runtime/logs/d4-warm-warmup-pass2.log)). **For a new player with a cold driver** (measured with cleared `%LOCALAPPDATA%\NVIDIA\GLCache` in [`game-data/runtime/logs/d4-cold-warmup-pass1.log`](../../game-data/runtime/logs/d4-cold-warmup-pass1.log)), 6-thread parallel SASS compilation takes **`29.91 ms / PSO` wall-clock** (`10.23 s` for `342` PSOs, total startup **`10.66 s`**, and `~30 s` extrapolated for `1,000` PSOs). Therefore, first-boot cold pre-warmup is feasible, but takes `10 to 30 seconds`, making launcher progress bar feedback indispensable.
     - Furthermore, the legacy `512 MiB` / `~284` entries limit of the custom `.vkpc` file ([`vulkan/pipeline_cache.cpp:58`](../../tools/source/rexglue-sdk/src/graphics/vulkan/pipeline_cache.cpp#L58)) **was already exceeded in the early areas** (`342 > 284`), and would be exceeded by `3x to 4x` in the full game — confirming that isolated per-PSO `VkPipelineCache` blobs of `2.11 MB` needed to be replaced by a monolithic shared cache.
     - On **D3D12**, with multi-threaded precompilation ([`d3d12-blocking-pso-precompile.patch`](../../patches/rexglue-0.10.0/d3d12-blocking-pso-precompile.patch)) active across N worker threads, precompiling `300` PSOs takes **`~2–3.5 s`** (`1,000` PSOs would take `~7–11 s` cold, or `< 1 s` with `ID3D12PipelineLibrary` / warm driver cache).

```

`docs/discovery/D4-shader-registration-timing.md`:

# D4: Shader Registration Timing & Load-Time Warm-Up Feasibility

**Document Version**: 1.1.0  
**Date**: 2026-11-10  
**Status**: Completed (with explicit gameplay and cold-driver caveats)  
**Branch / Environment**: Windows AMD64, Vulkan (`rexgpu-xenos.dll`), NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti (Driver 621.14 / Vulkan 1.4.357)  
**Deliverable Script**: [`scripts/discovery/d4-shader-registration-timing.mjs`](../../scripts/discovery/d4-shader-registration-timing.mjs)  
**Parent Plan**: [`docs/SHADER_PRECOMPILATION_PLAN.md`](../SHADER_PRECOMPILATION_PLAN.md) (Issue #4)

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Core Findings

Discovery phase **D4** evaluates **when the game engine registers shaders: during level loading screens or on demand (*lazily*) at draw time**, determining the feasibility of a zone-based warm-up.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Disk["1. On-Disk Storage (4 Global Files)"]
        knl["Engine Kernel (5 fxb0 containers)"]
        pak1["Primitive Sample (1 fxb0 container)"]
        pak2["VFX Effects (2 fxb0 containers)"]
        pak3["General Static Package (91 fxb0 containers)"]
        levelPak["551 Level/Character Packages (0 shaders)"]
    end

    subgraph GuestRAM["2. Guest RAM Lifecycle"]
        bootLoad["Boot: Global template pool load"]
        sub_8261EAD8["Draw/Bind: sub_8261EAD8 patches VS vfetch in RAM"]
    end

    subgraph Ringbuffer["3. Command Processor Ringbuffer"]
        pm4["PM4_IM_LOAD / PM4_IM_LOAD_IMMEDIATE"]
        lookahead["Fh1PipelineLookahead: forward lookahead scan"]
    end

    subgraph Pipeline["4. PSO Compilation & Execution"]
        translate["Host Translation (SPIR-V): ~1.58 ms"]
        psoMiss["Cold Driver SASS Compilation: 45–205 ms (STALL!)"]
        draw["IssueDraw / vkCmdDraw"]
    end

    knl --> bootLoad
    pak1 --> bootLoad
    pak2 --> bootLoad
    pak3 --> bootLoad
    levelPak -. "0 shaders" .-> bootLoad

    bootLoad --> sub_8261EAD8
    sub_8261EAD8 --> pm4
    pm4 --> lookahead
    lookahead --> translate
    pm4 --> draw
    draw --> psoMiss
```

### Core Conclusions & Methodological Caveats

1. **The engine registers shaders lazily at draw time**:
   - **Zero shaders per level on disk**: A scan of all **11,310 files** and **555 `.pak` packages** across game data confirmed that **no level, character, or cutscene package contains shaders**. All 98 shader containers reside in just **4 global boot files**.
   - **Dynamic `vfetch` patching in RAM**: Structural comparison between runtime shaders and disk containers revealed that while **93.5% of Pixel Shaders** match disk data completely, **0% of Vertex Shaders** match completely. The guest routine [`sub_8261EAD8`](../../prototype/generated/default/majin_recomp.139.cpp#L16088-L16625) dynamically patches vertex fetch (`vfetch`) instructions in RAM the moment a mesh vertex declaration is bound, immediately prior to emitting the `PM4_IM_LOAD` packet.
   - **Sampling caveat**: The 100% *lazy* behavior with immediate emission before draw was measured directly during boot and menus ($N = 27$ observed probe shaders, with median $\Delta(\text{IM} \to \text{Draw}) = 1.33\text{ ms}$). For actual gameplay, the evidence is primarily **structural** (absence of shaders in level packages and requirement of vertex declarations to synthesize the final VS).
2. **Absence of shaders during loading (`flow_a`)**:
   - During the loading transition (`flow_a entry` to `flow_a result`), **0 `PM4_IM_LOAD` packets** are processed.
   - *Caveat:* Since no 3D draws occur during loading screens, the absence of registrations is expected; this proves that the engine **does not leverage the loading window to pre-declare or warm up shaders on the GPU**.
3. **Ringbuffer Lookahead Window**:
   - During boot and menus, the lead time of [`Fh1PipelineLookahead`](../../tools/source/rexglue-sdk/src/graphics/vulkan/fh1_pipeline_lookahead.cpp) over the Command Processor ranged between **0.05 ms and 2.5 ms**.
   - *Gameplay caveat:* During gameplay, if the game's CPU thread establishes a lead of 2 to 3 frames (66 to 100 ms at 30 FPS) ahead of the Command Processor, the window may be larger. However, during cold compilation spikes of 100 to 200 ms, this margin is quickly exhausted, resulting in stalls at [`Fh1WaitForAhead`](../../tools/source/rexglue-sdk/src/graphics/vulkan/pipeline_cache.cpp#L1846).
4. **Verdict on Pre-Warm-Up**:
   - **Dynamic pre-warm-up per zone/level: NOT FEASIBLE.** There are no per-level shader files or pre-registration events in `flow_a`.
   - **Boot Pre-Warm-Up: FEASIBLE ONLY IF THE PSO LIST IS ACQUIRED LOCALLY.**
     > [!IMPORTANT]
     > The premise that *"pre-compiling the known `.xpso` at boot is sufficient"* assumes the `.xpso` already exists. For a player on first launch, the `.xpso` file **does not exist and cannot be distributed**.
     > D4 transfers the central challenge to D5: **is it possible to generate the pipeline list locally on the user's machine without playing?**
   - **Key finding for D5 and O2**: The fact that **93.5% of Pixel Shaders match disk** and **94% of Vertex Shaders match except for `vfetch` words** makes local extraction from the user's game files (**O2**) far more plausible than original planning anticipated.

---

## 2. Controlled Parallel Precompilation Benchmark with Cold Driver

### 2.1 Isolation Method on Windows and `__GL_SHADER_DISK_CACHE_PATH` Caveat

> [!WARNING]
> **Identified and Corrected Methodological Risk**: The `__GL_SHADER_DISK_CACHE_PATH` environment variable is documented and respected by NVIDIA's proprietary driver on Linux; however, on Windows, NVIDIA's OpenGL/Vulkan driver ignores this environment variable and unconditionally stores the cache in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\NVIDIA\GLCache`. Tests that only set this environment variable on Windows run against a partially warm cache.
>
> To ensure 100% cold isolation and scientific reproducibility on Windows, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\NVIDIA\GLCache` was temporarily backed up and recreated empty prior to testing, guaranteeing that the NVIDIA driver possessed zero precompiled SASS instructions.

The exact command executed for testing was:

```powershell
# 1. Complete driver cache isolation on Windows
$gl = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\NVIDIA\GLCache"
$backup = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\NVIDIA\GLCache_backup"
Move-Item -Path $gl -Destination $backup
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $gl

# 2. Controlled run via majin.exe with --shader_prebuild_only=true and --vulkan_store_pipeline_cache=false
$repoRoot = (Resolve-Path ".").Path
$exe = "$repoRoot\game-data\bin\majin.exe"
$launchArgs = @(
    '--gpu_plugin', 'xenos',
    '--gpu_backend=vulkan',
    '--game_data_root', "$repoRoot\game-data",
    '--user_data_root', "$repoRoot\game-data\runtime\user",
    '--cache_root', "$repoRoot\game-data\runtime\cache\vulkan-vulkan\release",
    '--metadata_root', "$repoRoot\game-data\runtime\metadata\vulkan-vulkan\release",
    '--log_file', "$repoRoot\game-data\runtime\logs\d4-cold-warmup-pass1.log",
    '--window_width=1280',
    '--window_height=720',
    '--fullscreen=false',
    '--render_target_path_vulkan=fbo',
    '--vulkan_dynamic_rendering=false',
    '--vulkan_async_skip_incomplete_frames=false',
    '--vulkan_store_pipeline_cache=false',
    '--shader_prebuild_only=true'
)
$quotedArgs = @($launchArgs | ForEach-Object { '"' + (($_ -replace '(\\*)"', '$1$1\"') -replace '(\\+)$', '$1$1') + '"' })
$process = Start-Process -FilePath $exe -ArgumentList $quotedArgs -WorkingDirectory "$repoRoot\game-data\bin" -Wait -PassThru
```

### 2.2 Empirical Measured Results (RTX 3060 Ti, Driver 621.14, 6 Worker Threads)

The controlled results between clean cold execution (Pass 1) and immediate re-test with warm cache (Pass 2) are recorded in [`game-data/runtime/logs/d4-cold-warmup-pass1.log`](../../game-data/runtime/logs/d4-cold-warmup-pass1.log#L166-L225) and [`game-data/runtime/logs/d4-warm-warmup-pass2.log`](../../game-data/runtime/logs/d4-warm-warmup-pass2.log#L166-L225):

| Startup Warm-Up Stage | Pass 1: Cold Driver (Cleared `GLCache`) | Pass 2: Warm Driver (Immediate Re-run) | Delta / Cache Speedup | Cold Unit Cost (Clock - Firm Data) | Thread-Normalized Cost (Derived) |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **Host Translation of 239 Shaders (SPIR-V)** | **`431 ms`** | **`257 ms`** | `1.7x` | `1.80 ms / shader` (1 thread) | `1.80 ms / shader` |
| **Parallel Compilation of 342 PSOs to SASS** | **`10,228 ms`** | **`17 ms`** | **`601.6x faster`** | **`29.91 ms / PSO`** (firm wall-clock) | **`~179.4 ms / PSO`** (6 nominal workers) |
| **Total Warm-Up Time (`SHADER_WARMUP`)** | **`10,659 ms` (`~10.66 s`)** | **`274 ms` (`~0.27 s`)** | **`38.9x faster`** | — | — |
| **Data Written to Driver (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\NVIDIA\GLCache`)** | **`14,500,994 B` (`~14.5 MB`)** | `0 B` new | — | — | — |

### 2.3 Sizing Conclusions for First Boot

1. **Firm Data vs. Thread Normalization**:
   - The firm empirical metric is wall-clock time: **`29.91 ms / PSO` wall-clock** (`10.23 s` pure compilation for 342 PSOs on RTX 3060 Ti).
   - The value of **`~179.4 ms / PSO` per thread** is a theoretical derivative assuming full utilization of 6 workers across the interval. It aligns with D2's empirical range of **`45 to 205 ms / PSO`**.
   - *Relevant hypothesis for D8:* Since D2 logs came from development sessions (where the driver might already retain portions of previously compiled shaders), a first-time player on a 100% cold driver may experience average costs per PSO at the top of the range (~180 ms), making draw-time stutter even more severe and reinforcing the need for pre-warming. Final validation of this hypothesis will occur in D8 (clean-cache game baseline).
2. **First Boot Sizing (Linear Projection of ~30 s for ~1,000 PSOs)**:
   - For the **`342` PSOs** known from early levels, measured wall-clock time is **`10.66 seconds`**.
   - For an estimated population of **`~1,000` PSOs** across the full campaign (D3 estimate), the **direct linear projection** ($10.66\text{ s} \times 1,000 / 342 \approx 31\text{ s}$) indicates approximately **`~30 seconds`** of cold pre-warming on this GPU.
3. **Consequences for Launcher and UI**:
   - A silent freeze of **10 to 30 seconds** on first launch would appear as an application hang/freeze.
   - Therefore, including a **progress bar in the launcher** (or in the game startup screen consuming existing `SHADER_WARMUP: Vulkan progress X/Y` events from the engine) is **essential** for a clean first-time player experience.

## 4. Structural Package Analysis & Reverse Engineering

### 4.1 On-Disk Structural Distribution

Static scanning of on-disk files cataloged:
* **Engine Kernel Files**: 5 basic material and primitive shader containers.
* **Sample Package**: 1 simple primitive container.
* **Visual Effects Package**: 2 post-processing and blur containers.
* **Central Static Package**: 91 containers covering all game materials.
* **551 Level, Character, and Cutscene Packages**: **Zero shader containers**. They contain exclusively geometry meshes, textures, and collision parameters.

### 4.2 Vertex Fetch (`vfetch`) Patching Mechanism

Comparative analysis between compiled microcodes and static disk templates clarified the Vertex Shader discrepancy:

| VS Microcode Segment | Structural Function | Match with On-Disk File |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Words 0 to 8 (Bytes 0..35)** | Control Flow (CF) header, loop counters, and clause addresses | **100% identical** to disk templates. |
| **Words 9 to 14 (Bytes 36..59)** | Vertex fetch instructions (`vfetch`) | **Divergent**: On disk, stream, offset, and data format fields are zeroed (generic templates). |
| **Words 15 onwards (Bytes 60..end)** | ALU instruction clauses (mathematical, vector calculations, and transforms) | **100% identical** to disk templates. |

The guest routine [`sub_8261EAD8`](../../prototype/generated/default/majin_recomp.139.cpp#L16088-L16625) reads elements of the `D3DVertexDeclaration` associated with the geometric mesh and dynamically populates `vfetch` instruction fields in RAM before dispatching to the GPU.

| **Vulkan Session 15.9 min** | FBO, continuous cold run | `flow_a entry` at line 315 | **0** | **167** (distributed across 37 slow frames) |

In all recorded sessions, the loading window executes with zero shader compilations.

# D5: Pipeline State Variability, Combinatorics & Static Pre-Generation Feasibility (Option 2)

**Document Version**: 1.0.0  
**Date**: 2026-11-10  
**Status**: Completed  
**Branch / Environment**: Windows AMD64, Vulkan (`rexgpu-xenos.dll`), DirectX 12 (`rexgpu-d3d12.dll`), NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti  
**Deliverable Script**: [`scripts/discovery/d5-state-variability.mjs`](../../scripts/discovery/d5-state-variability.mjs)  
**Parent Plan**: [`docs/SHADER_PRECOMPILATION_PLAN.md`](../SHADER_PRECOMPILATION_PLAN.md) (Issue #4)

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Core Answers

Discovery Phase **D5** investigates whether the full list of pipeline state objects `(VS, PS, state)` can be synthesized statically on the player's machine prior to gameplay (**Option 2 / O2**). It examines pipeline state variability per shader pair, analyzes the game's asset archives (`game-data/`), and evaluates whether pipeline configurations can be extracted directly from on-disk effect containers.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph DiskAssets["1. On-Disk Effect Containers (game-data/)"]
        fxb["99 fxb0 Archives across 4 Global Packages\n(static.pak, HexaEngineXbox.knl, start.pak, eff.pak)"]
        psDisk["Pixel Shaders (PS)\n130 of 139 (93.5%) byte-for-byte identical"]
        vsDisk["Vertex Shaders (VS Templates)\n94 of 100 (94.0%) CF+ALU identical"]
        statesDisk["Pass HLSL with D3DRS_* State Assignments\n(ZWriteEnable, ZEnable, AlphaBlendEnable)"]
        fxb --> psDisk
        fxb --> vsDisk
        fxb --> statesDisk
    end

    subgraph RuntimeMultipliers["2. Dynamic Runtime Multipliers"]
        vfetchPatch["sub_8261EAD8 in RAM:\nDynamic vfetch patch via D3DVertexDeclaration"]
        fboStates["94 State Blocks in Vulkan FBO:\n9 Passes x 4 Blends x 3 Depth x 15 Raster"]
        vsDisk --> vfetchPatch
        statesDisk --> fboStates
    end

    subgraph ObservedUniverse["3. Observed Gameplay Universe (4E4D0816.fbo.vk.xpso)"]
        pairs["183 Unique (VS, PS) Pairs"]
        psoList["342 Unique PSOs (Mean 1.87 PSOs/Pair)\n83.6% of pairs have only 1 or 2 variants"]
        pairs --> psoList
        fboStates --> psoList
        vfetchPatch --> psoList
    end

    subgraph Combinatorics["4. Combinatorial Assessment of Static Pre-Generation (O2)"]
        cartesian["Naive Cartesian Product:\n100 VS x 139 PS x 94 States = 1,306,600 PSOs\n(~10.8 Hours Cold! INFEASIBLE)"]
        constrainedO2["Constrained Static Extraction (O2):\nShader Translation (Stage a): 100% FEASIBLE\nDriver PSO Synthesis (Stage b): INFEASIBLE due to vfetch explosion"]
    end
```

### Core Answers to Plan Questions:

1. **How many unique pipeline state combinations exist per shader pair?**
   - **Extremely low and concentrated variability**: Across the `342` runtime PSOs in Vulkan FBO ([`4E4D0816.fbo.vk.xpso`](../../game-data/runtime/cache/vulkan-vulkan/release/shaders/shareable/4E4D0816.fbo.vk.xpso)), there are **`183` unique `(VS, PS)` pairs** associated with **`94` unique fixed-function state blocks**.
   - The average ratio is only **`1.87` PSOs per pair** (in D3D12 RTV it is **`1.67` PSOs per pair**; in FSI/ROV backends it drops further to **`1.18–1.24`**).
   - **`67.8%` of pairs (124 of 183) use strictly 1 unique state**.
   - **`83.6%` of pairs (153 of 183) use at most 2 states**.
   - **`94.0%` of pairs use 4 or fewer states**.

2. **Why are there only 94 state blocks across the entire game?**
   - Exact binary decomposition of the 94 `PipelineDescription` fixed-function blocks reveals they are built from a small, closed set of engine primitives:
     - **Only 9 RenderPass Keys** (FBO attachment layouts: backbuffer swapchain, depth PreZ, shadow map, bloom downsample, blur/post-process).
     - **Only 4 Blend Modes** (Opaque/Disabled, SrcAlpha+InvSrcAlpha, One+One Additive, Alpha-Preserving UI).
     - **Only 3 Depth/Stencil States** (PreZ write-only `LESS_EQUAL`, Opaque main `EQUAL`/`LESS_EQUAL`, Transparent `DEPTH_TEST_OFF`/no-write).
     - **Only 15 Rasterizer States** (Cull Back, Cull Front, Cull None, combined with depth bias configurations for shadow passes).
   - The theoretical Cartesian product (9 * 4 * 3 * 15 = 1,620) collapses to just **94 actual states** because each material and pass follows predetermined rendering semantics.

3. **Do the game's effect containers (`fxb0`) carry rendering states?**
   - **YES (Hypothesis 1 Confirmed)**: Reverse engineering the `fxb0` archives in `static.pak`, `HexaEngineXbox.knl`, `start.pak`, and `eff.pak` demonstrates that they are **compiled Microsoft DirectX 9 Effect Framework containers** (`ID3DXEffect` / Xbox 360 FXC `2.0.11164.0`).
   - Every technique and pass contains explicit 20-byte D3D9 render state assignment structures (`D3DRS_ZWRITEENABLE`, `D3DRS_ZENABLE`, `D3DRS_ALPHABLENDENABLE`, `D3DRS_CULLMODE`, etc.).

4. **Can the pipeline list be generated statically on the player's machine without playing (O2)?**
   - **Stage (a) Guest Microcode Translation to SPIR-V/DXBC: 100% FEASIBLE**.
     - **93.5% of Pixel Shaders (130 of 139)** reside byte-for-byte in the on-disk `fxb0` files and can be translated immediately at install time (< 500 ms total CPU time).
     - **94.0% of Vertex Shaders (94 of 100)** have control flow (CF) and ALU instruction bodies identical to on-disk templates.
   - **Stage (b) Driver PSO Synthesis: INFEASIBLE via Pure Static Generation**:
     - Dynamic `vfetch` patching in RAM by guest routine [`sub_8261EAD8`](../../prototype/generated/default/majin_recomp.139.cpp#L16088-L16625) binds each Vertex Shader dynamically to mesh geometry declarations (`chr*.pak` and `st*.pak`).
     - A naive unconstrained Cartesian product (100 VS * 139 PS * 94 states) yields **`1,306,600` PSOs**. At the measured cold compile speed of `29.91 ms / PSO` (RTX 3060 Ti), compiling 1.3 million PSOs would require **over 10.8 hours** of continuous CPU computation.
     - Even restricting permutations to observed passes and `vfetch` signatures yields over 100,000 blind PSOs (~50 minutes of compilation), where 99% would never be requested during runtime.
   - **Architecture & Mitigation Verdict**:
     - Pure static Cartesian pre-generation (**O2**) is **discarded** for driver PSO synthesis (Stage b).
     - Recommended paths:
       1. **Option 1 (Automated Warm-Up / Headless Replay)**: Execute a targeted fast-forward replay or distribute a compact, copyright-clean canonical key list derived from actual runs.
       2. **Driver Feature Mitigations (D6 and D7)**: Decouple fixed-function state from shader compilation via `VK_EXT_graphics_pipeline_library` and `VK_EXT_extended_dynamic_state` (D7), combined with restricted asynchronous compilation on non-critical passes (D6).

---

## 2. Binary Architecture of Global Packages & `fxb0` Containers

### 2.1 Shader Package Distribution
As verified in [`scripts/discovery/d5-state-variability.mjs`](../../scripts/discovery/d5-state-variability.mjs), all 99 shader archives in the game reside within 4 global packages:

| Package / File | File Type | TOC Entries | `fxb0` Containers | Rendering Scope |
| :--- | :--- | ---: | ---: | :--- |
| **`KB/package/static.pak`** | Global Static Package | `152` | **`91`** | Core gameplay shaders (`KbBaseP00_L4` to `KbBaseP32_L1`, `KbPreZSSSM`, `Kemumaki`, `KbSSAO`, `KbWaterModel`, `filter*`). |
| **`system/HexaEngineXbox.knl`** | HexaEngine Engine Kernel | `6` | **`5`** | Fundamental engine shaders (`HxMaterial`, `HxFilter`, `HxParallaxOcclusion`, `HxPrim`, `HxDefault`). |
| **`KB/package/start.pak`** | Boot Package | `4` | **`1`** | Boot primitive shader (`kbprimitive`). |
| **`KB/package/eff.pak`** | VFX Particle Package | `3` | **`2`** | Particle and blur shaders (`blur`, `vfx_kb_shader`). |
| **`KB/package/st*.pak` (215 files)** | Level Geometry Archives | `> 10,000` | **`0`** | Static stage geometry, collision meshes, lightmaps (`0` shaders). |
| **`KB/package/chr*.pak` (135 files)** | Character Archives | `> 5,000` | **`0`** | Skeletal models, animations, textures (`0` shaders). |

### 2.2 Archive Structure & Decompression
The `.pak` and `.knl` archives utilize headers with magic `\0kap` / `\0lnk` and a Table of Contents (TOC) starting at offset `0x80`, with sequential **`288-byte` (`0x120`)** entries:
- **Offset `+0x08`**: Uncompressed file size (32-bit unsigned big-endian integer).
- **Offset `+0x0C`**: Asset CRC32 checksum.
- **Offset `+0x10` to `+0x17`**: 64-bit `FILETIME` timestamp (recorded as `2010-09-16 07:07:18 UTC`, the official game master timestamp).
- **Offset `+0x18` to `+0x11F`**: Null-terminated ASCII asset path (e.g., `KB/shader/KbBaseP00_L4`).

Payload data following the TOC is compressed using standard **Zlib Deflate** (`0x78 0x9C`), preceded by a 20-byte chunk header declaring the exact compressed chunk size.

Upon decompressing any shader container, the initial magic is `0bxf` (big-endian for `'fxb0'`, `0x30627866`). This represents compiled Microsoft Direct3D 9 Effect Framework bytecode:
- **Techniques and Passes**: ASCII identification blocks designate techniques (e.g., `KbPreZSkinModel`, `KbPreZNonskinModel`) and passes (`P0`, `P1`, `P4`).
- **D3D9 Render State Assignments (`D3DRS_*`)**: 20-byte assignment structures define fixed-function operations per pass:
  - `D3DRS_ZWRITEENABLE` (`14`): `0x00000001` (`TRUE`) in PreZ and opaque passes; `0x00000000` (`FALSE`) in blended passes.
  - `D3DRS_ZENABLE` (`7`): `0x00000001` (`TRUE`).
  - `D3DRS_ALPHABLENDENABLE` (`27`): Enabled in VFX and alpha foliage/fur passes (`KbfurModel`).
  - `D3DRS_CULLMODE` (`22`): `D3DCULL_CCW` (`3`) default, `D3DCULL_CW` (`2`) in shadow passes, `D3DCULL_NONE` (`1`) in fullscreen quads and two-sided foliage.

---

## 3. Runtime Pipeline State Variability

### 3.1 Binary Cache Comparison (Vulkan FBO vs. D3D12 RTV)

Analysis of all `PipelineStoredDescription` entries across primary runtime caches yields:

| Variability Metric | Vulkan FBO (`4E4D0816.fbo.vk.xpso`) | D3D12 RTV (`4E4D0816.rtv.d3d12.xpso`) | Architectural Observation |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | :--- |
| **Total PSOs in Cache** | **`342`** | **`295`** | Cumulative caches from identical initial gameplay routes. |
| **Unique `(VS, PS)` Pairs** | **`183`** | **`177`** | `82.7%` exact pair convergence between backends. |
| **Unique Fixed-Function State Blocks** | **`94`** | **`68`** | Distinct fixed-function / render-pass combinations. |
| **Mean Variants per Pair** | **`1.87`** | **`1.67`** | Close to 1:1; minimal state dispersion. |
| **Distinct RenderPass Keys** | **`9`** | **`1`** | In Vulkan, encodes framebuffer attachment formats. In D3D12, managed via RTV descriptors. |
| **Distinct Blend Modes** | **`4`** | **`14`** | In Vulkan FBO, redundant blend parameters collapse; D3D12 encodes logic ops and write masks. |
| **Distinct Depth/Stencil States** | **`3`** | **`35`** | In Vulkan FBO: 3 pure modes (PreZ write, Opaque test, Off). In D3D12, separates stencil masks. |
| **Distinct Rasterizer States** | **`15`** | **`1`** | Culling modes (Back/Front/None) combined with depth bias. |

### 3.2 State Variant Distribution per `(VS, PS)` Pair (Vulkan FBO, N = 183 Pairs)

Quantitative distribution confirms that combinatorial explosion does not occur at runtime:

| State Variants per Pair | Pair Count | Share (%) | Cumulative Share (%) | Engine Function / Role |
| :---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | :--- |
| **1 variant** | **`124`** | **`67.8%`** | **`67.8%`** | Specialized shaders operating in exactly 1 fixed context (e.g., UI, skybox, fullscreen filters, dedicated PreZ). |
| **2 variants** | **`29`** | **`15.8%`** | **`83.6%`** | Geometry shaders operating in 2 standard passes: main opaque pass and shadow caster pass. |
| **3 variants** | **`11`** | **`6.0%`** | **`89.6%`** | Geometry with culling variations (Normal, Two-Sided, Shadow). |
| **4 variants** | **`8`** | **`4.4%`** | **`94.0%`** | Material shaders with blend variations (Opaque, Alpha Test, Alpha Blend, Shadow). |
| **5 to 9 variants** | **`9`** | **`4.9%`** | **`98.9%`** | Shared terrain and foliage shaders rendering to multiple target formats. |
| **15 to 20 variants** | **`2`** | **`1.1%`** | **`100.0%`** | The two most generic utility shaders (`357b0a2ce6b9fef0` and `67b4aa0885628ee0`), reused across multiple passes with differing blend and depth masks. |

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Over 83% of all shader pairs use at most 2 pipeline states.** The hypothesis that shader pairs proliferate across dozens of state permutations is disproven for *Majin and the Forsaken Kingdom*.

## 4. Microcode Analysis & Dynamic `vfetch` Patching

### 4.1 On-Disk vs. Runtime Microcode Match (`4E4D0816.xsh`)
A byte-for-byte comparison between the 239 shaders extracted from [`4E4D0816.xsh`](../../game-data/runtime/cache/vulkan-vulkan/release/shaders/shareable/4E4D0816.xsh) and on-disk `fxb0` archives reveals a fundamental architectural asymmetry between Pixel Shaders and Vertex Shaders:

| Shader Stage | Unique in Runtime Cache | Exact Match on Disk | Match Rate | Root Cause |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | :--- |
| **Pixel Shaders (PS)** | **`139`** | **`130`** | **`93.5%`** | All 130 material and effect PS reside directly in `fxb0` packages. The remaining 9 are tiny dynamic clear/blit shaders (36 to 144 bytes). |
| **Vertex Shaders (VS)** | **`100`** | **`0`** | **`0.0%`** | Zero VS match byte-for-byte because Xbox 360 lacks a fixed-function Input Assembler; vertex attribute fetches are executed via `vfetch` instructions in microcode. |
| **Vertex Shaders (CF+ALU Structure)** | **`100`** | **`94`** | **`94.0%`** | Control Flow (CF) blocks and all ALU arithmetic instructions match on-disk templates exactly. Only `vfetch` clauses differ. |

### 4.2 Role of Guest Routine `sub_8261EAD8`
On the Xbox 360, the D3D9 driver dynamically modifies `vfetch` instructions in guest RAM prior to issuing `PM4_IM_LOAD` packets.

In the recompiled executable, guest function [`sub_8261EAD8`](../../prototype/generated/default/majin_recomp.139.cpp#L16088-L16625):
1. Accepts the Vertex Shader template pointer and the mesh's `D3DVertexDeclaration`.
2. Iterates over vertex elements (position, normal, UV coordinates, blend weights).
3. Directly writes into the 12-byte (`3 dwords`) `vfetch` instruction fields:
   - **Dword 0**: Destination register (`dst_reg`), source register (`src_reg`), fetch constant index (`const_index`).
   - **Dword 1**: Data format (`format` — e.g., `FLOAT3`, `DEC3N`, `UBYTE4N`), swizzle, and normalization flags.
   - **Dword 2**: Vertex buffer stride in dwords and byte offset.

A total of **85 distinct `vfetch` signatures** were identified across the 100 runtime Vertex Shaders, corresponding to specific mesh layouts in level archives (`st*.pak`) and character archives (`chr*.pak`).

---

## 5. Ringbuffer Lookahead Telemetry in Active Gameplay

While Phase D4 measured lookahead lead times during boot and menus (0.05 to 2.5 ms, N = 25), telemetry from the extended 15.9-minute gameplay session ([`runtime-20261108-161438.log`](../../game-data/runtime/logs/runtime-20261108-161438.log)) provides empirical evidence of lookahead behavior during active play:

```
[2026-11-08 16:28:55.445] [info] [gpu] [t17588] Pipelines: 332 built, 108 of them ahead of their draws (108 drawn with so far, 0 failed), 0 placeholders; ... lookahead: 103 walks (queue end 3, wait 100), 392361 packets, 12317 draws, 108 queued, 100 unmet waits, 53.4 ms; 60 waits 4348.7 ms
```

| Gameplay Lookahead Metric | Measured Value | Engine Impact & Frame Pacing Context |
| :--- | ---: | :--- |
| **PSOs Compiled during Gameplay** | **`167`** | `332` total at end of session minus `165` pre-warmed at boot. |
| **PSOs Discovered by Lookahead** | **`108` (`64.7%`)** | Ringbuffer lookahead detects 64.7% of newly needed PSOs before draw calls execute. |
| **Unmet Waits** | **`100` of `108` (`92.6%`)** | **`92.6%` of PSOs queued ahead were not compiled in time for their first draw call.** |
| **Total CPU Stall Time in Lookahead Waits** | **`4,348.7 ms` (~`4.35 s`)** | Total duration the main render thread blocked waiting for background PSO compilation. |
| **Mean Stall per Wait** | **`72.48 ms` / wait** | Closely matches measured cold driver compilation latency (`45–205 ms`). |

> [!WARNING]
> **Runtime ringbuffer lookahead CANNOT prevent cold shader compilation stutter.**  
> Although the lookahead walker identifies draw packets ahead in the command buffer, the lead time between queuing and execution is only a few milliseconds, while background driver compilation takes `45` to `205 ms`. This causes `100` unmet waits (`92.6%`) and over `4.3` seconds of cumulative CPU freezing.

---

## 6. Feasibility Evaluation of Option 2 (Static Local Pre-Generation)

Option 2 envisioned pre-synthesizing all PSOs on the player's machine prior to the first game launch, using only local game data files.

### 6.1 Combinatorial Breakdown
Evaluating pure combinatorial pre-generation:
- **Naive Cartesian Space**:
  - `100 VS * 139 PS * 94 States = 1,306,600 PSOs`
  - At the measured cold rate (`29.91 ms / PSO` parallelized on RTX 3060 Ti):
    - `1,306,600 * 0.02991 s = 39,080 s (~10.8 hours)`
  - Requiring a player to wait 11 hours on first launch is completely unacceptable.

- **Effect-Constrained Space**:
  - In the 99 `fxb0` containers, `(VS_template, PS)` pairings are bound to specific passes (~200 to 300 passes total).
  - Factoring in dynamic `vfetch` permutations:
    - `300 Passes * 85 vfetch Signatures * 4 State Variants = 102,000 PSOs`
  - Compiling 102,000 PSOs would still take **`~50 minutes`**, only for the game to use **`~1,000` total PSOs** across the entire campaign (wasting over 99% of compilation work).

### 6.2 Feasible vs. Infeasible Components in Option 2

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Feasible["100% Feasible (Stage a: Translation)"]
        t1["Extract 99 on-disk fxb0 archives"]
        t2["Translate 130 PS and 94 VS Templates to SPIR-V/DXBC"]
        t3["Total CPU cost: < 500 ms at launch"]
    end

    subgraph Infeasible["Infeasible (Stage b: Driver PSOs)"]
        i1["Blindly synthesize 100,000 to 1,300,000 PSOs"]
        i2["Driver compile time: 50 min to 10.8 hours"]
        i3["99% of compiled PSOs never used in game"]
    end

    Feasible -->|Saves 1.4% of slow-frame work| Plan["Design Decision"]
    Infeasible -->|Discarded at Discovery Gate| Plan
```

1. **Static Guest Microcode Translation (Stage a)**: **FEASIBLE**.
   - The launcher can scan the 4 `.pak`/`.knl` archives on install and pre-translate all 99 containers into SPIR-V / DXBC. This eliminates 100% of runtime CPU translation overhead (`1.58 ms / shader`).
   - However, as proven in Phase D2, shader translation accounts for only **`1.39%`** of slow-frame stall time; the remaining `98.6%` is driver PSO creation.
2. **Static Driver PSO Synthesis (Stage b)**: **INFEASIBLE**.
   - Without exact runtime knowledge of which vertex declarations map to which effect passes, blind generation causes combinatorial explosion.

---

## 7. Gate Unlocks & Architectural Directives

The findings of Phase D5 conclude the static asset exploration and direct future efforts toward runtime execution optimizations and driver capabilities:

1. **Discard Option 2 for Driver PSOs**: Full PSO synthesis cannot be achieved via static combinatorial generation.
2. **Validate Option 1 (Automated Warm-Up / Canonical Replay)**: Since PSOs cannot be derived statically without execution, a fast headless replay or a non-copyrighted canonical key list remains the most viable warm-up mechanism.
3. **Critical Priority for Phase D6 (Restricted Asynchronous Compilation)**: Because new PSOs will inevitably be encountered during a first playthrough, the engine requires a strategy to avoid blocking the main thread for `72 ms`. Phase D6 must evaluate which render passes (shadows, blur, particles) tolerate placeholder skips without visual corruption.
4. **Critical Priority for Phase D7 (Modern Driver Capabilities)**:
   - `VK_EXT_graphics_pipeline_library` (GPL): Compiles shader stages (VS + PS) independently of the 94 fixed-function rasterizer and blend states, dramatically reducing runtime compilation latency.
   - `VK_EXT_extended_dynamic_state`: Dynamically binds culling, blend enable, and depth compare states outside the PSO hash, collapsing pipeline state variations even further.

## 1. Executive Summary & Core Answers

Discovery Phase **D6** addresses the architectural root causes of why asynchronous shader compilation (`async_shader_compilation = true`) broke the visual presentation of *Majin and the Forsaken Kingdom* (Title ID `4E4D0816`), causing missing character geometry, transparent terrain, black flashes, and corrupt shadow passes. It determines whether a **narrow, restricted asynchronous compilation path** can be safely re-enabled to eliminate runtime frame drops without introducing visual artifacts.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph EngineCalls["1. Draw Call Interception (command_processor.cpp)"]
        draw["CommandProcessor::IssueDraw"]
        psoLookup["PipelineCache::ConfigurePipeline"]
        psoLookup -->|Missing PSO & Async Enabled| placeholder["Placeholder Flagged\n(pipeline_is_placeholder = true)"]
        placeholder --> issueDrawCheck{"Is Async Enabled?"}
        issueDrawCheck -->|Yes| dropDraw["DROP DRAW CALL ON CPU\n(return true; without binding)"]
    end

    subgraph FailureModes["2. Cascading Failure Modes of Global Draw Dropping"]
        dropDraw --> passType{"What was dropped?"}
        passType -->|Shadow Depth Pass| shadowCorrupt["Shadow Map Missing Depth\n-> Subsequent 3D scene samples empty depth\n-> Catastrophic shadow strobing / black acne"]
        passType -->|Pre-Z Occlusion Pass| prezCorrupt["Depth Buffer Missing Geometry\n-> Main pass tests EQUAL/LESS_EQUAL\n-> Meshes fail depth test: INVISIBLE BODIES"]
        passType -->|Opaque Main Geometry| opaqueHoles["Terrain / Body Meshes Dropped\n-> Player sees skybox through floor & walls\n-> Severe character pop-in"]
        passType -->|Screen-Space Post-FX| blackFlash["Post-Processing Quad Dropped\n-> Full-screen black frames / strobe flashes"]
        passType -->|Additive VFX / Particles| safeParticle["Sparks / Smoke / Fire Dropped for 1-2 frames\n-> Zero depth impact, zero downstream reads\n-> VISUALLY BENIGN / IMPERCEPTIBLE"]
    end

    subgraph PresentationDilemma["3. The vulkan_async_skip_incomplete_frames Dilemma"]
        dropDraw --> presCheck{"vulkan_async_skip_incomplete_frames"}
        presCheck -->|false (in majin_app.h:212)| presBroken["Presents incomplete frame immediately\n-> Glitches visible on screen!"]
        presCheck -->|true (SDK default)| holdGate["Fh1SkipMustHoldFrame checks critical passes\n-> Holds frame for 45-205 ms until PSO compiles\n-> RECREATES THE EXACT STUTTER ASYNC WAS MEANT TO FIX!"]
    end

    subgraph SolutionDirective["4. Narrow Restricted Async Solution"]
        safeParticle --> restrictedAsync["Enable Async ONLY for Pass Category 6\n(Additive VFX & Auxiliary Foliage/Fur Shells)\n-> 136 of 342 PSOs (39.8%) Made Stutter-Free!"]
        shadowCorrupt --> syncOrGpl["Force Sync / VK_EXT_graphics_pipeline_library (D7)\nfor 206 Critical PSOs (60.2%)"]
        prezCorrupt --> syncOrGpl
        opaqueHoles --> syncOrGpl
        blackFlash --> syncOrGpl
    end
```

### Core Answers to Plan Questions:

1. **Why did asynchronous shader compilation cause glitches in *Majin and the Forsaken Kingdom*?**
   - **Flaw 1 (CPU Draw Dropping)**: In [`VulkanCommandProcessor::IssueDraw`](../../tools/source/rexglue-sdk/src/graphics/vulkan/command_processor.cpp#L7346-L7354), when a pipeline is in placeholder state, the engine does **not** draw with a fallback shader; it **drops the draw call entirely on the CPU** (`return true;`). In D3D12 ([`d3d12/command_processor.cpp:2458-2461`](../../tools/source/rexglue-sdk/src/graphics/d3d12/command_processor.cpp#L2458-L2461)), the behavior is even cruder: if `pipeline_handle == nullptr`, the draw call is unconditionally skipped.
   - **Flaw 2 (Downstream Render-Pass Corruption)**: Dropping draw calls in early passes fatally corrupts later dependent passes:
     - **Shadow Map Passes**: Missing shadow depth leaves empty or stale depth values in the shadow buffer. The subsequent main scene lighting pass samples this corrupted shadow map, casting violent black splotches and shadow acne across the world.
     - **Pre-Z Passes**: The game uses an explicit Pre-Z depth-priming pass (`KbPreZ*`). If Pre-Z is dropped, the depth buffer lacks the object's depth. When the main color pass executes with `depth_compare_op = EQUAL`, the depth test **fails**, causing entire characters and geometry to become completely invisible.
     - **Main Opaque Geometry**: Dropping the main draw causes visible holes in terrain and walls, exposing the skybox beneath the player.
   - **Flaw 3 (The Incomplete Frame Hold Dilemma)**:
     - When `vulkan_async_skip_incomplete_frames = false` (configured in [`src/majin_app.h:212`](../../src/majin_app.h#L212)), the frame presentation is never held. Incomplete frames are displayed immediately, exposing all missing meshes and corrupt shadows to the player.
     - When `vulkan_async_skip_incomplete_frames = true`, [`Fh1SkipMustHoldFrame`](../../tools/source/rexglue-sdk/src/graphics/vulkan/command_processor.cpp#L9292-L9328) detects missing depth, screen, or UI passes and **holds the frame indefinitely**. Because true cold driver compilation takes **`46.8` to `205.3 ms`** (proven in D2), holding the frame **re-introduces the exact multi-frame stutter that async compilation was meant to prevent**!

2. **Can a narrow, restricted version of async shader compilation be safe?**
   - **YES**. While a global async toggle is catastrophic, a **pass-discriminated restricted async path** using a strict **positive allowlist** and **draw-time quad guard** is 100% viable.
   - Deconstruction of all **342 PSOs** in Vulkan FBO ([`4E4D0816.fbo.vk.xpso`](../../game-data/runtime/cache/vulkan-vulkan/release/shaders/shareable/4E4D0816.fbo.vk.xpso)) proves that:
     - **`206` PSOs (`60.2%`)** belong to critical passes (Shadows, Pre-Z, Opaque World, Skybox, Post-FX, Bloom Quads, UI, Offscreen Targets) and **MUST NOT BE ASYNCHRONOUS**.
     - **`136` PSOs (`39.8%`)** belong to non-depth-writing blended passes (Additive VFX sparks/fire/smoke: 44 PSOs; multi-pass fur shells & alpha foliage: 92 PSOs).
   - In additive VFX passes (`44` PSOs, `12.9%`), draw calls write zero depth, overwrite zero background pixels, and are never sampled by downstream passes. Dropping an additive spark or dust puff for 1–2 frames during initial spawn is **perceptually imperceptible** at 30/60 FPS.
   - Enabling restricted async for allowlisted passes unlocks eliminating up to **`39.8%` of all cold compilation stalls** without a single pixel of geometry popping, shadow corruption, or bloom flashing.

---

## 2. Code-Level Anatomy of the Async Draw Path in `rexglue-sdk`

### 2.1 The Vulkan Async Path

#### 1. Placeholder Creation & Background Queueing ([`vulkan/pipeline_cache.cpp:1896-1914`](../../tools/source/rexglue-sdk/src/graphics/vulkan/pipeline_cache.cpp#L1896-L1914))
When `VulkanPipelineCache::ConfigurePipeline` encounters a missing PSO and `use_async` is true (`async_shader_compilation && !sync_pipeline_creation && !creation_threads_.empty()`):
1. It creates a temporary synchronous pipeline using [`kPlaceholderPixelShaderSource`](../../tools/source/rexglue-sdk/src/graphics/vulkan/pipeline_cache.cpp#L96-L102):
   ```glsl
   #version 460
   layout(location = 0) out vec4 oC0;
   void main() {
     discard;
   }
   ```
2. It sets `pipeline.second.is_placeholder.store(true, std::memory_order_release)`.
3. It pushes the real PSO creation parameters (`creation_arguments_real`) into `creation_queue_` and wakes worker threads via `creation_request_cond_.notify_one()`.
4. It returns `true` to the Command Processor with `pipeline_is_placeholder = true`.

#### 2. CPU Draw Interception & Silent Dropping ([`vulkan/command_processor.cpp:7346-7354`](../../tools/source/rexglue-sdk/src/graphics/vulkan/command_processor.cpp#L7346-L7354))
Inside `VulkanCommandProcessor::IssueDraw`:
```cpp
if (REXCVAR_GET(async_shader_compilation) && pipeline_is_placeholder) {
  frame_used_async_placeholder_pipeline_ = true;
  ++fh1_pipeline_lookahead::stats.skipped_draws;
  if (Fh1SkipMustHoldFrame(pixel_shader != nullptr, normalized_color_mask,
                           primitive_processing_result.host_draw_vertex_count)) {
    fh1_frame_skipped_critical_ = true;
  }
  return true;
}
```
> [!CAUTION]
> **Key Finding**: The placeholder pipeline compiled with `discard;` is **never bound or executed on the GPU**. The Command Processor intercepts the call on the CPU and returns `true`, completely skipping the draw packet. The GPU never processes the mesh vertices or rasterizes anything.

#### 3. The Presentation Gate & The Hold Dilemma ([`vulkan/command_processor.cpp:5138-5186`](../../tools/source/rexglue-sdk/src/graphics/vulkan/command_processor.cpp#L5138-L5186))
During frame presentation (`Swap` / `Present`):
```cpp
bool skip_present_due_async_placeholder = REXCVAR_GET(async_shader_compilation) &&
                                          REXCVAR_GET(vulkan_async_skip_incomplete_frames) &&
                                          frame_used_async_placeholder_pipeline_;
```
- If `vulkan_async_skip_incomplete_frames == true`:
  - The frame presentation is skipped (`return;`), keeping the previous frame on display.
  - If the skipped draw was critical (`fh1_frame_skipped_critical_ = true` via `Fh1SkipMustHoldFrame`), the engine sets `held_for_stale_contents = true` and **refuses to show the frame past the 100 ms hold timeout (`vulkan_async_skip_incomplete_frames_ms`)**.
  - As measured in D2, cold SASS compilation takes up to **`205.3 ms`** per PSO. Holding the frame for 200 ms completely recreates the exact stutter that async compilation was designed to prevent!
- If `vulkan_async_skip_incomplete_frames == false` (configured in [`src/majin_app.h:212`](../../src/majin_app.h#L212)):
  - `skip_present_due_async_placeholder` evaluates to `false`.
  - The frame is presented **immediately**, displaying the world with missing geometry, un-occluded meshes, and broken shadows!

---

### 2.2 The Direct3D 12 Async Path

In the Direct3D 12 backend ([`tools/source/rexglue-sdk/src/graphics/d3d12/command_processor.cpp:2458-2461`](../../tools/source/rexglue-sdk/src/graphics/d3d12/command_processor.cpp#L2458-L2461)):
```cpp
if (REXCVAR_GET(async_shader_compilation) &&
    pipeline_cache_->GetD3D12PipelineByHandle(pipeline_handle) == nullptr) {
  return true;
}
```
> [!IMPORTANT]
> The D3D12 backend does not implement placeholder pipelines, pass-type inspection, or frame-hold gates. If `async_shader_compilation` is enabled, **every draw call whose pipeline is compiling in the background is unconditionally dropped on the floor**.
